target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` for installed-agent, workspace-file, partial-state, and package-reference visibility
- add read-only `claws remove <claw-or-agent> --dry-run --json` planning
- require separate `--yes` consent before removing the Claw-created agent and owned state
- delete only unchanged managed workspace files and preserve local edits
- release skill/plugin provenance without uninstalling shared artifacts
- retain the install ledger when cleanup becomes unsafe after the agent config commit

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names may resolve an install when unambiguous; final agent ids are always accepted and are required when the same package has created multiple agents.

Remove revalidates the agent config digest and managed files before mutation. Agent config drift and unsafe workspace paths block the plan. Missing files are treated as already removed, locally modified files are retained while their managed reference is released, and unchanged files are deleted through the existing rooted filesystem helper. Package references are released only after cleanup completes; the underlying skill/plugin remains installed.

If file cleanup becomes unsafe after the agent entry is removed, successful file-reference cleanup is retained but the root install and package references remain, so `status` and later doctor work can explain and retry the partial removal.

All commands remain process-gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and all new JSON contracts report `stability: "experimental"`.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102228 package installation and references
- This PR: lifecycle visibility and conservative cleanup
- Next: #102306 exports the portable state now represented by the ledger

This stage introduces removal only after agent, file, and package ownership are recorded well enough to plan cleanup without deleting unrelated state.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- focused Oxlint on all seven changed files
- 18 focused status/remove and CLI tests
- 7 Claw lifecycle E2E tests, including real add/status/remove round trip

target.title: Add experimental Claw lifecycle diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

- add an experimental core doctor check that projects the existing Claw lifecycle status model into structured health findings
- report partial installs, missing or modified agents, managed workspace drift, MCP ownership drift, and unresolved cron ownership
- detect subordinate workspace/package/MCP/cron rows that have no root Claw install record
- keep the check and ordered doctor contribution completely absent unless OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1

## Contract

- doctor reuses claws status ownership states instead of independently hashing or interpreting managed resources
- complete package references and complete cron scheduler references are not treated as errors without an authoritative live verifier
- unreadable lifecycle state returns one structured error finding rather than crashing doctor
- diagnostics are advisory and do not mutate config, files, scheduler state, or provenance

## Verification

- pnpm tsgo:core
- focused Oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors across 6 touched files
- 114 focused collector, core-check, and doctor-contribution tests
- real CLI proof: with the experiment disabled, --only core/doctor/claws-state is unknown; enabled mode reports a modified SOUL.md from a real Claw add ledger

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #102406 MCP ownership
- This PR: read-only lifecycle and drift diagnostics
- Next: #102959 uses the same ownership model for grouped update planning

Doctor lands after every add/remove owner so it can reuse one authoritative status model instead of inventing partial resource checks. The Claws CLI and doctor surface remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

target.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents
target.body:
## Summary

- install version-pinned ClawHub skills into the newly created agent workspace
- install version-pinned ClawHub plugins through the existing shared plugin lifecycle
- record one root SQLite package reference after each successful install
- preserve successful package references and return a partial add result if a later install fails
- expose Claw references through the shared uninstall-warning path used by CLI, Gateway, and Control UI; warn, but do not take away operator control

## Scope

This is the package slice of the experimental Claw lifecycle. It keeps the grouped RFC contract (`packages[].kind`, `source`, `ref`, and exact `version`) and deliberately does not restore the earlier generic artifact selectors or agent skill lists. MCP servers and cron jobs remain blocked for later stack slices.

Package installation runs after agent/config creation and managed workspace files. Skills use the existing ClawHub skill installer with the new agent workspace; plugins use the existing ClawHub plugin installer and its normal safety/config behavior. References describe Claw dependency provenance, not exclusive ownership: uninstall remains an operator-controlled action, and later Claw removal will release references without automatically removing shared packages. The shared warning helper also keeps the Control UI plugin-management path in #103176 aligned with CLI lifecycle behavior.

The CLI remains process-gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` in the base of this stack.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #101973 managed workspace files
- This PR: package installation and shared dependency provenance
- Next: #102296 makes installed ownership visible and removable

This stage comes after workspace creation because skills install into that new agent workspace, and before status/remove because those commands need package references to explain shared ownership.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`
- focused Oxlint on all seven changed files
- 22 focused package, provenance, and plugin-uninstall tests
- 6 Claw lifecycle E2E tests
